exposure: Transperineal ultrasound (TPU) measurement of anteroposterior mid-pelvic diameter (AMD)
outcome: Agreement and reliability of TPU vs MR pelvimetry measurements
cohort: The participants were 67 nulliparous women with a singleton fetus in breech presentation who received both TPU and MR pelvimetry.
finding: Transperineal ultrasound (TPU) can accurately and reliably measure the anteroposterior mid-pelvic diameter (AMD), and a smaller AMD is significantly associated with an increased risk of intrapartum cesarean section in attempted vaginal breech birth.
mod_finding: A smaller anteroposterior mid-pelvic diameter (AMD) was associated with an increased risk of intrapartum cesarean section when vaginal breech birth was attempted, suggesting TPU could aid women in deciding their preferred mode of birth.
